**Source:** Kevin L. Clark, "On 'Gemini Rights' Steve Lacy Gets Personal About Red Flags & Trusting His Instincts," Grammy.com, July 12, 2022

**Not in the article:** John Carroll Kirby, Ely Rise, Dahi, and Diana Gordon are not mentioned. Fousheé is the only collaborator named. The article also doesn't explain the album's title, and it doesn't directly compare the album to *Apollo XX1* (the article's spelling).

**Lacy's quotes on the album's making**

*Concept and emotional core*
- "_Gemini Rights_ is essentially me coming into myself after a breakup." (Story of the album)
- "I'm finding myself after a heartbreak and I am excited for people to hear this record." (Story of the album)

*Fousheé and "Sunshine"*
- "It wasn't transactional in any way." (On working with Fousheé)
- "She found me when I was in a slump about what to do next" (On how they met)
- "The way that we'd work is by writing, and then when a new idea pops up, we'd just sing together on two mics." (Process)
- "It'd get up to about 20 minutes long" (On freestyle sessions, before being edited down)
- "You might as well just be on this song. Just be the only feature on my album." (On making Fousheé the only feature)
- "it has all of this anger and animosity towards the person who affected me" (On "Sunshine")

*Family vocals*
- "They sing the 'la-la' part on 'Helmet.'" (On "Helmet")
- "I got them on 'Amber,' singing on the big swell when the bass comes in." (On "Amber")
- "They're all on that part." (On "Give You The World," where the family sings the "goodbye" part; the article has the wording as "I then added them to 'Give You The World,'")

*Approach and growth*
- "I learned with this album two things: the superpower of editing and that you got to make trash." (Lesson learned)
- "I would treat [Gemini Rights] like how a rapper would and that made it way more fun." (Approach)
- "I'm going to get better on the next one" (On his growth as a songwriter and producer)

*Independence and label*
- "I was really happy being independent for a while" (On moving to RCA)

**Interviewer narration (not Lacy's words)**
- Kevin L. Clark describes the album as "majorly self-produced by Lacy" with only one guest appearance.
- Clark says the album is "an even more personal offering than his 2019 debut solo effort, _Apollo XX1_."
- Clark notes Lacy's "Sunshine" comments were shared with Apple Music 1's Zane Lowe.

- "I used my mom and my sisters on my last album, on the track 4ever."

*Context:* Lacy explains that his mother and sisters appear on the record. He first used them on the track "4ever" from his previous album and says the new record needed that texture.

**Interviewer narration:** Lacy says he hit a wall working alone and so brought other people in, making a deliberate effort to be more open to their input. **Lacy's quotes**

- "This is the first time I consciously said I was an artist."
- "I thought I was just a guitar player. I thought I was just a producer, a vessel to help other people."

*Context:* Lacy reflects that before this album he saw himself mainly as a guitarist and producer. He says he is now comfortable calling himself an artist.

---

### Title Origin

**Lacy's quotes**

- "I was just in a bar with my homegirls in New York and I heard someone say 'gay rights'."
- "I kept saying it as a joke."
- "I had the name before I even had the songs written."

*Context:* Lacy explains that the title is a sardonic riff on "gay rights." The Gemini persona then gave the album a theme.

**Interviewer narration:** The article describes Gemini as one of the zodiac's most divisive signs and notes that Lacy himself doesn't put much stock in astrology.

---

### Breakup

**Lacy's quotes**

- "It's a fucking break-up album."
- "I was just in the studio, grinding and writing through all the anger, all the sadness."

*Context:* Lacy describes the album as a response to ending a relationship with his boyfriend.

**Interviewer narration:** The article says the breakup happened in August 2021 and that the album is positive and philosophical about the relationship, not bitter.

Lacy's direct quotes about individual tracks are limited to "Amber," "Helmet," "Give You the World," and "Sunshine," which are covered in the narration above. The article doesn't include a direct Lacy quote about "Sunshine."

- "I wanted to sound like a girl because I love women's voices."

*Context:* Lacy explains that he sings some falsetto parts in a way meant to sound like a woman, and that he finds women's voices comforting.

### Previous Album: *Apollo XXI*

**Lacy's quotes:** None on this album in the article.

**Interviewer narration:** The article says Lacy released his debut album, *Apollo XXI*, two years after his 2017 solo project *Steve Lacy's Demo*.

---

### Death Theme

**Lacy's quotes**

- "I thought I'd died. It scared the shit out of me."
- "Death," he said, when asked what gets him out of bed in the morning.
- "The realisation that death defines the meaning of your life."
- "I look at my life as a museum, like experiences that I collect."
- "I think music is an opportunity to tell a story and create a thread for someone else to continue."
- "That's what keeps it fun, because this won't be for ever."

*Context:* After a near-fatal car crash in June 2020, Lacy says the experience shifted his priorities. He describes wanting his music to leave a lasting thread for others after he's gone.

**Interviewer narration:** The article describes the crash as a head-on collision on a single-lane mountain road near Lacy's home in Los Angeles. Lacy walked away with only a few cuts on his hands.

## Background and Recording

- **Fousheé session:** Per the article, Lacy played the instrumental for Fousheé. They spent about 20 minutes freestyling over it, which led to verses and a chorus melody. The article doesn't name a source for this detail.
- **Revisions:** Over the following year, Lacy changed elements including the ending breakdown, the drums, and the chorus.
- **Completion:** Per Lacy, the song was finished a week before he submitted *Gemini Rights* to RCA. Source: Shaad D'Souza, *The Guardian*, December 22, 2022, https://www.theguardian.com/music/2022/dec/22/my-mom-thinks-im-doing-drugs-but-im-at-home-baking-cookies-steve-lacy-on-his-breakout-year.
- **Recording span:** June 2021–June 2022 (infobox).

## Lacy's Direct Quotes

- GQ (Gordon, June 23, 2022): the "renaissance" quote above. Lacy also said he intended the a cappella section to sound like he was "singing directly to" the listener.
- The Guardian (D'Souza, December 22, 2022): Lacy described the lyrics as "a play on confidence." He said the narrator moves from feeling not good enough to feeling "almost too good" but "still down."
- The Guardian (same piece): Lacy initially found the official sped-up version "gross" but agreed to it in hopes of helping the song reach No. 1.
- Rolling Stone (Jeff Ihaza, October 20, 2022, https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/steve-lacy-bad-habit-grammy-preview-1234607474/): Lacy said the refrain represents fans wanting something from him that he didn't realize he had.

- **Writing changes:** Tyler, the Creator suggested changing the chorus wording to make it "more memorable." Lacy adopted the change, which removed a repeated word from the original chorus line. - **Producer:** Steve Lacy.
- **Mixing:** Neal Pogue at Hot Purple Petting Zoo studio, Los Angeles. Pogue mixed the guitar riff as the song's main focus (Paul Tingen, *Sound on Sound*, December 2022, https://www.soundonsound.com/techniques/inside-track-steve-lacy-bad-habit).

- Key of F minor, tempo 84–88 BPM, vocal range C4–C6 (sheet music, Musicnotes, August 1, 2022).

- Structure: three parts, with an a cappella section and a jazz-fusion-style breakdown.

content.text:
## ① 대상·조사 범위

- **대상**: Steve Lacy, *Gemini Rights*. 2022-07-15 발매, 10곡, 총 34:57(S7). 표기 레이블은 "℗ 2022 L-M Records, under license to RCA Records"(S3)입니다.
- **판본**: 지정 판본은 Spotify ID `3Ks0eeH0GWpY4AU20D5HPD`입니다. Spotify 페이지는 열지 못했습니다. 그래서 이 ID와 Apple Music 표준판(10곡, 약 35분)이 같은 판본인지는 직접 대조하지 못했습니다.
  - Wikipedia에는 표준판만 있고 디럭스판 기재는 없습니다.
  - 〈Bad Habit (Sped Up)〉은 앨범 판본이 아니라 별도 파생 음원입니다(S9).
  - 6번 트랙 제목은 Genius·Wikipedia에서 "2Gether (Enterlude)"이고, 일부 소매점에서는 "2gether - Interlude"입니다.
- **기준일**: 2026-10-16(접근일 2026-10-20).
- **열지 못한 곳**: genius.com, theguardian.com, gq.com(도구 차단), whosampled.com(403), billboard.com(tollbit 리디렉트, 미추적).
  - 그래서 GQ·Guardian·Billboard·Rolling Stone 발언은 Wikipedia를 거친 [재인용]입니다.
  - Zane Lowe 인터뷰 원본(Apple Music 1)이나 전사본은 확보하지 못했습니다.
- **조사 범위 밖**: 부클릿 원본, 프로듀서 Ely Rise·Dahi·John Carroll Kirby 본인의 작업 설명은 이번 조사에서 찾지 못했습니다.
- **후속 자료**: 2026년 앨범 *Oh yeah?*는 오너가 이미 보유한 자료여서 다시 설명하지 않습니다.

## ② 핵심 근거 (중요도순)

**C1. 이별 이후를 다룬 작품이라는 자기 설명** — [직접 발언·원문 확인] S1, S2
- 라시는 "Gemini Rights is essentially me coming into myself after a breakup"(S1), "It's a fucking break-up album"(S2)이라고 말했습니다.
- 이별 시점(2021년 8월)과 상대가 남자친구였다는 내용은 S2 기자의 서술입니다.
- **한계**: 창작자의 자기 설명일 뿐 작품이 그 주제를 구현했다는 근거는 아닙니다. 가사 화자를 실제 인물과 동일시하지 않습니다.

**C2. 혼자 하던 방식에서 협업으로 전환** — 층위가 서로 달라 나눕니다.
- C2a [보도·원문 확인] S2: 혼자 하다 한계에 부딪혀 다른 사람을 들였다는 내용은 기자의 서술이고, 직접 인용문이 아닙니다.
- C2b [보도·원문 확인] S6: 전작 *Apollo XXI*는 믹싱까지 혼자 했고, 이번에는 공동 작곡자·프로듀서·연주자·엔지니어·외부 믹서를 들였다는 내용도 기자(Paul Tingen)의 서술입니다.
- C2c [직접 발언·원문 확인] S2: "This is the first time I consciously said I was an artist… I thought I was just a guitar player… just a producer." 이는 자기 인식에 관한 발언이고, 작업 범위에 관한 진술은 아닙니다.
- **한계**: 무엇을 혼자 했는지는 작곡·프로듀싱·연주·믹싱 가운데 '믹싱' 정도만 S6 기자 서술로 특정됩니다.

**C3. 프로듀싱 지분에 대한 자기 평가** — [직접 발언·재인용] S4, S5
- Zane Lowe 인터뷰를 옮긴 인용입니다: "I produced about 90% of the record, still." 그리고 "I tried to be like, 'Oh, I need an executive producer…' But I ended up still doing it."
- **한계**: 비율은 본인의 표현이지 크레딧에서 계산한 값이 아닙니다. Genius에서 라시가 프로듀서로 등재된 트랙이 8/9곡(Sunshine 제외)이라는 사실과 같은 것으로 취급하지 않습니다.

**C4. 편집 중심의 작업 방식과 곡 수** — 층위가 서로 달라 나눕니다.
- C4a [직접 발언·원문 확인] S1: "the superpower of editing and that you got to make trash." Fousheé와의 즉흥 작업은 "about 20 minutes long"까지 늘어난 뒤 잘라냈다고 했습니다.
- C4b [보도·원문 확인] S2: 2년 동안 300곡 넘게 만들어 10곡으로 추렸다는 내용은 기자의 서술입니다.
- C4c [직접 발언·재인용] S4: "10 songs", "get in, get out."

**C5. 〈Bad Habit〉 제작 경과** — [보도/직접 발언·재인용] S8
- 2021년 6월 처음 녹음했습니다. Fousheé와 약 20분 동안 즉흥으로 만든 결과에서 벌스와 후렴 멜로디가 나왔습니다. 이후 1년 동안 엔딩 브레이크다운, 드럼, 후렴을 수정했습니다(Wikipedia 서술이며 출처 미표기).
- 앨범을 RCA에 제출하기 1주일 전에 완성했습니다(Guardian, 재인용).
- Tyler, the Creator의 제안으로 후렴 가사를 바꿨습니다(Billboard, 재인용).
- 아카펠라 구간은 듣는 사람에게 "singing directly to" 하듯 들리도록 의도했다고 했습니다(GQ, 재인용).
- **한계**: 원문 3건을 모두 열지 못했습니다. Fousheé 세션 대목은 Wikipedia에 출처가 붙어 있지 않습니다.

**C6. 크레딧 상충: Kirby·Ely Rise의 역할** — [DB등재·상충] S9 ↔ S7·S8
- Genius에는 Kirby가 프로듀서 6/9, 작곡·작사 6/9로, Ely Rise가 프로듀서 5/9, 작곡·작사 5/9로 등재돼 있습니다(S9).
- Wikipedia 트랙표에서 Kirby의 작곡 크레딧은 Static·Bad Habit·2Gether 3곡뿐입니다. 나머지 곡에서 그의 역할은 신시사이저와 오르간이며, 프로듀서는 라시(2Gether는 Matt Martians)로 적혀 있습니다(S7).
- 〈Bad Habit〉의 라이너 노트 인용에서도 Kirby는 "songwriting, additional synths"이고 프로듀서는 라시 단독입니다(S8).
- Yuli(Genius 10번 작곡)는 Wikipedia에 없습니다. Denise Stoudmire(Wikipedia 10번 백보컬)는 Genius 요약에 없습니다.
- **판단**: 해결되지 않았으므로 핵심 논거로 쓰지 않습니다. 부클릿 대조가 필요합니다.

**C7. 가족 보컬 배치** — [직접 발언·원문 확인] S1, S2
- 라시가 직접 위치를 밝혔습니다. 〈Helmet〉은 "la-la" 부분, 〈Amber〉는 "the big swell when the bass comes in", 〈Give You the World〉는 "goodbye" 부분입니다(S1).
- 전작의 〈4ever〉에서 어머니·누이를 썼다는 것과 "I like the texture of women's voices"도 직접 발언입니다(S2).
- Genius의 Background Vocals 등재(2·8·10번)와 트랙 단위로 일치합니다. 이는 [교차 확인]입니다.

**C8. Fousheé의 비중** — [보도·원문 확인]와 [DB등재]가 상충
- S4 기자는 Zane Lowe 인터뷰를 근거로 앨범의 "roughly half"를 Fousheé와 함께 썼다고 서술했습니다. 직접 인용문은 아닙니다.
- 작곡 크레딧은 Wikipedia에서 4/10곡(3·5·7·9번), Genius에서 3/9곡입니다(9번 제외).
- 피처링은 〈Sunshine〉 하나입니다. "Just be the only feature on my album"(S1, 직접 발언)입니다.
- **한계**: 크레딧 곡 수로 실제 기여량을 계산하지 않습니다.
